'''Alexandru Dan Ionescu''' is a mathematician and academic who serves as a professor of mathematics at [[Princeton University]].

Ionescu's research primarily focuses on [[Partial differential equation|partial differential equations (PDEs)]] and [[mathematical physics]]. He is a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]], a member of the American Academy of Sciences and Letters, and was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2022.

==Education and career==
Ionescu earned his [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in mathematics from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1995. He then obtained both his [[M. A.|M.A.]] in mathematics in 1997 and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in mathematics in 1999 from [[Princeton University]].<ref name = tuff>{{Cite web|url=https://web.math.princeton.edu/~aionescu/CV.html|title=CV|website= Princeton University|access-date=September 15, 2025}}</ref>

Ionescu held postdoctoral appointments at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] and the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. In 2002, he joined the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] as an assistant professor, was promoted to associate professor in 2005, and became a full professor in 2008. Since 2010, he has served as a professor at [[Princeton University]].<ref name = tuff/>

==Works==
Ionescu's research spans analysis and partial differential equations, with applications to mathematical physics. His work has addressed questions of global [[Well-posed problem|well-posedness]] for nonlinear dispersive equations, including the [[Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation|KP-I equation]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Klein |first1=C. |last2=Saut |first2=J.-C. |title=Numerical Study of Blow up and Stability of Solutions of Generalized Kadomtsev–Petviashvili Equations |journal=Journal of Nonlinear Science |date=1 October 2012 |volume=22 |issue=5 |pages=763–811 |doi=10.1007/s00332-012-9127-4 |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00332-012-9127-4 |language=en |issn=1432-1467|url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[Schrödinger equation|Schrödinger maps]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chousionis |first1=Vasilis |last2=Erdoğan |first2=M. Burak |last3=Tzirakis |first3=Nikolaos |title=Fractal solutions of linear and nonlinear dispersive partial differential equations |journal=Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society |date=2015 |volume=110 |issue=3 |pages=543–564 |doi=10.1112/plms/pdu061 |url=https://doi.org/10.1112/plms/pdu061 |language=en |issn=1460-244X|arxiv=1406.3283 }}</ref> the [[Benjamin–Ono equation]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pub.uni-bielefeld.de/record/3000863|title=On well-posedness of Benjamin-Ono type equations|website=Universitat Bielefeld|access-date=September 7, 2025}}</ref> and [[Dispersion (water waves)|water waves]]<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1002/cpa.21711|title=Global Infinite Energy Solutions for the 2D Gravity Water Waves System|first1=Xuecheng|last1=Wang|journal=Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics|volume=71|issue=1|pages=90–162|date=2018|doi=10.1002/cpa.21711|via=Wiley|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Ionescu has also made contributions to [[harmonic analysis]], particularly in [[ergodic theory]], where he proved extensions of the Furstenberg–Bergelson–Leibman conjecture to the [[Nilpotent|nilpotent setting]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bourgain |first1=Jean |author-link=Jean Bourgain |last2=Mirek |first2=Mariusz |last3=Stein |first3=Elias M. |author-link3=Elias M. Stein |last4=Wright |first4=James |title=On a multi-parameter variant of the Bellow–Furstenberg problem |journal=Forum of Mathematics, Pi |date=January 2023 |volume=11 |pages=e23 |doi=10.1017/fmp.2023.21 |url=https://doi.org/10.1017%2Ffmp.2023.21 |language=en |issn=2050-5086|doi-access=free }}</ref> His research further encompasses kinetic and [[Plasma modeling|plasma models]], including stability<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Velozo Ruiz |first1=Anibal |last2=Velozo Ruiz |first2=Renato |title=Small Data Solutions for the Vlasov–Poisson System with a Repulsive Potential |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |date=13 March 2024 |volume=405 |issue=3 |pages=80 |doi=10.1007/s00220-024-04970-3 |url=https://doi.org/10.1007%2Fs00220-024-04970-3 |language=en |issn=1432-0916|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and scattering results for the [[Vlasov equation|Vlasov–Poisson system]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bigorgne |first1=Léo |title=Modified scattering for the small data solutions to the Vlasov–Maxwell system |journal=Journées équations aux dérivées partielles |date=22 July 2024 |pages=1–15 |doi=10.5802/jedp.673 |url=https://doi.org/10.5802%2Fjedp.673 |language=en |issn=2118-9366|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In addition, his work in [[general relativity]] includes proving [[Rigidity (mathematics)|rigidity]] results for [[Kerr metric|Kerr black-hole solutions]] to the [[Einstein field equations|Einstein vacuum equations]] under specific geometric and analytic assumption.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gómez-Lobo |first1=Alfonso García-Parrado |last2=Senovilla |first2=José M. M. |title=A set of invariant quality factors measuring the deviation from the Kerr metric |journal=General Relativity and Gravitation |date=1 June 2013 |volume=45 |issue=6 |pages=1095–1127 |doi=10.1007/s10714-013-1518-9 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10714-013-1518-9 |language=en |issn=1572-9532|arxiv=1211.6884 }}</ref>
